teaches: How to run a 184-frame scene on one held body pose: Gumball and Darwin sit tangled on a lawn in front of a photographic suburban fence, limbs bound up together with grey bands, both gripping the same green-cased phone, and for ~160 frames almost nothing moves except their faces -- rage, strain and shouted insults cycle through the face-comp system (2,683 face kf against 1,680 body kf) while the grapple itself is a single sustained strain. The payoff is saved for the last ~24 frames: Darwin's expression flips to delight, the tangle breaks, he exits frame-right with the prize and Gumball is left toppling backwards, dazed. A shouting match is a face scene; the bodies just have to hold the tension.
notes: A layer literally named 'ROUGH' ships inside the clean production file (V007), empty of placements -- the rough stage was cleared but its layer was never deleted.
The background is a genuine photographic plate (suburban houses, lattice fence, lawn, sky) named GB204_PHONE_SC154_LO_BG.jpg; the puppets are flat vector over it.

Both puppets sit on their own scene layers (GB200_GUMBALL_PUPPET_STD_001 / GB200_DARWIN_STD_PUPPET_001, 18 keyframes each) -- the grapple is posed inside the puppets, not choreographed at scene level.
The grapple holds for ~160 of 184 frames; the release (Darwin delighted, Gumball toppling) takes only the last ~24 frames, and Darwin exits frame-right in the final frames.
